The arrivals lead discussed a reminder about airflow checks after a rushed handover. Incident report on a missed connection with a companion animal.

The traveler arrived at the Companion Animal Travel Desk with a calm but urgent concern after a connection was missed during transfer handling. The pet crate had been accepted without issue at the first point of contact, and the traveler had received clear guidance before departure. During the handoff, the workflow became crowded, and the team noticed that the crate routing note had not been passed along in the usual order. That gap led to a delay in moving the traveler and pet to the correct departure stream. The senior coordinator was notified right away, and the safety coordinator reviewed the handling area for any other lapse that could affect companion travel.

<<FACT F116>>

The desk team separated the traveler record from the baggage flow and confirmed that the pet remained secure and comfortable. A new escort was arranged, and the traveler was kept informed in plain language throughout the process. Staff also checked the crate label, the transport status, and the station handoff log to make sure the missed connection was documented clearly. The handling note was updated so the next team would see the issue before any further transfer.

<<FACT F110>>

After the immediate response, the senior coordinator asked for a quick debrief with the staff involved. The main point was that rushed handovers should never skip the airflow check or the routing confirmation, even when the line is busy. The safety coordinator also asked for a short refresher on companion animal transfer steps, with extra attention on clear verbal handoff and a second look at all crate tags. The traveler was told that the case would stay open until the follow-up review was complete and the service record was corrected. This was handled as a process failure, and the team was reminded to keep every transfer steady and documented.
